title: Settings like the registry
description:
Store typed settings in a tree of keys and values, as the registry does.

```
set HKCU\Software\Xenon\Window Width = 1280 (DWORD)
set HKCU\Software\Xenon\Window Title = "Editor" (SZ)
get Width as DWORD -> 1280
get Title as DWORD -> ERROR_INVALID_DATATYPE
delete key Window -> its values go too
```
hints: Walk the path one part at a time with `children[part]` to create, or `find` to read (lesson 5.02).
`std::get_if<std::uint32_t>(&value)` returns `nullptr` when the type is different.
requirements: Keys are paths split at `\`; each key has values of type DWORD, QWORD or string.
Reading a value with the wrong type is an error, like `RegGetValue` with a type filter.
Export the tree as text in `.reg` style.
stretch: Make key names case-insensitive like the real registry.
